name: Dish/EchoStar spectrum programme
spectrum: 700 MHz E-block, AWS-4 (2 GHz), H-block, AWS-3 via DEs, 600 MHz, CBRS, 3.45 GHz
cost_basis: >$30B cash incl. >$10B DE investments; $37.5B incl. capitalized interest (2023-06-30)
outcome_value: ~$42.6B headline sales (AT&T $23B; SpaceX $17B + $2.6B) plus ~$2B SpaceX-funded interest; remaining licences unvalued
lesson: A nominal gain, but below a normal cost of capital. The sale was forced by FCC build-out scrutiny and debt, and two strategic buyers set the price. Equity jumped 430% only after the 2025 deals, and subsidiaries still filed Chapter 11.

name: TerreStar/DBSD 2 GHz converted to AWS-4, sold to SpaceX
outcome_value: ~$17B (+~$2B interest support); about half in SpaceX stock
lesson: The biggest win came when the FCC changed the allowed use from satellite-only to terrestrial (2012) and, much later, a satellite direct-to-device buyer appeared. The original MSS backers had gone bankrupt.

name: Dish 600 MHz + 3.45 GHz sold to AT&T
outcome_value: ~$23B ($20.25B to EchoStar, $2.4B to an FCC trust)
lesson: Nationwide low and mid-band sold above cost when a large carrier needed capacity, but the buyer pool was essentially one carrier, and part of the price went to Dish's liabilities.

name: Dish DE unpaired AWS-3 sold to SpaceX
outcome_value: ~$2.6B in SpaceX stock
lesson: Unpaired, uplink-only spectrum without a device ecosystem sold at a deep discount under regulatory pressure.

name: NextWave C-block PCS
outcome_value: ~$5.4B of licence sales (Verizon ~$3.0B; Cingular $1.4B; Verizon NY $930M; MetroPCS $43.5M)
lesson: The bid was an overpayment at a peak. The licence value survived only through bankruptcy law and a court win against the FCC, and it took nine years.

name: NextWave Wireless sold to AT&T
cost_basis: Not confirmed (started with $550M cash in 2005, plus later debt)
outcome_value: Up to $600M from AT&T, mostly to retire debt; $25M (+$25M contingent) to shareholders
lesson: A technology bet (WiMAX) and interference-limited WCS spectrum left equity near zero. The operator bought cheaply once the rules eased.

name: Clearwire 2008 strategic investors
holder: Intel, Google, Comcast, Time Warner Cable, Bright House
cost_basis: $3.2B cash (~$20/share entry; entry price from prior knowledge)
outcome_value: Sprint buyout at $5/share
lesson: Deep spectrum holdings did not rescue a weak business model built on the losing technology (WiMAX).

name: Sprint, then T-Mobile, 2.5 GHz
cost_basis: $5/share for the Clearwire minority (~$14B implied Clearwire value)
outcome_value: Became T-Mobile's main 5G mid-band layer after the 2020 merger (prior knowledge); not separately valued
lesson: Value went to the scaled operator that deployed the spectrum years later, not to the original holders.

name: LightSquared (Harbinger)
spectrum: L-band MSS with ancillary terrestrial component (~1.5-1.6 GHz)
outcome_value: Equity effectively wiped out; Chapter 11 in 2012 (assets $4.48B, debts $2.29B)
lesson: An FCC conditional approval for terrestrial use was reversed over GPS interference. Entrenched incumbent users can veto a change of use.

name: Ligado L-band leased to AST SpaceMobile
cost_basis: ~$8.6B funded debt at the 2025 Chapter 11 (weak source)
outcome_value: $550M cash (mostly to Inmarsat) + >= $80M/yr usage payments
multiple: ~0.06x on cash; ~0.15x incl. PV of fees (estimate)
lesson: Even with a 2020 FCC approval (prior knowledge), defence and GPS opposition kept terrestrial use unviable. The satellite buyer paid lease fees, not a scarcity premium.

name: Straight Path Communications
cost_basis: Small spin-off market value (not verified this session)
outcome_value: $3.1B Verizon all-stock deal ($184/share); 20% of proceeds to the Treasury; ~$614M total settlement payments
lesson: A two-buyer bidding war at the peak of 5G mmWave enthusiasm set the price, and the regulator took a large cut.

name: Verizon as buyer of Straight Path mmWave
outcome_value: Auction 103 (2020) priced 37/39/47 GHz at ~$0.007/MHz-pop (prior knowledge); Verizon's 5G shifted to C-band
lesson: Paying a scarcity price for a band that turned out to be abundant and short-range destroyed value.

name: UK 3G auction
outcome_value: UK 4G auction in 2013 raised ~GBP2.34B for 250 MHz; large operator write-downs (prior knowledge)
lesson: Auction fever plus bubble financing. The Treasury captured the value, and licence prices later reset far lower.

name: German 3G auction
holder: Deutsche Telekom, Mannesmann/Vodafone, E-Plus, Viag/O2, Quam, MobilCom
outcome_value: Quam and MobilCom abandoned ~EUR8.4B licences each; 2010 auction ~EUR4.4B; 2019 5G ~EUR6.55B (prior knowledge)
lesson: Two of six winners walked away. Peak-cycle auctions transfer wealth to the state.

name: US mmWave auctions 101/102/103
outcome_value: Limited deployment; mid-band became the 5G workhorse
lesson: Huge supply relative to usable coverage. Abundant bands do not hold scarcity value.

name: C-band satellite incumbents
holder: SES, Intelsat, Eutelsat, Telesat, Star One
outcome_value: ~$9.7B accelerated relocation payments (SES ~ $4.0B, Intelsat ~ $4.9B; prior knowledge)
lesson: Lobbying for a regulatory repurposing paid the incumbents. The Treasury captured most of the value (Auction 107 ~$81B gross), not speculators.

name: Verizon C-band purchase
cost_basis: ~$45.5B bids; ~$53B incl. relocation and clearing (prior knowledge)
outcome_value: Network capacity gained; share price below its February 2021 level (prior knowledge, unverified)
lesson: Spectrum needed to run the network is not the same as shareholder value; there was no pricing power in a three-player market.

name: Globalstar
spectrum: Big LEO MSS 1.6/2.4 GHz; Band 53 terrestrial
outcome_value: FCC terrestrial authority 2016; Apple capacity deal 2022 and Nov 2024 $1.5B package incl. 20% equity stake (prior knowledge)
lesson: One anchor customer can monetize MSS spectrum, but that customer captures much of the value; terrestrial Band 53 stayed small.

name: Iridium
holder: Motorola-led Iridium LLC, then the 2000 buyer group
outcome_value: Assets bought out of bankruptcy for ~$25M in 2000; later re-listed and grew (prior knowledge)
multiple: ~0.005x for original backers; very large for 2000 buyers
lesson: Distressed buyers, not the original backers, captured the value, and the asset was a network as much as spectrum.

name: Anterix (pdvWireless) 900 MHz
cost_basis: Bought from Sprint in 2014 (~$90M per prior knowledge; unverified)
outcome_value: FCC 2020 realignment to broadband; utility lease deals; later strategic review (prior knowledge)
lesson: The regulatory upgrade succeeded, but a narrow buyer pool (utilities) slowed monetization.

name: ICO Global / TerreStar original backers
outcome_value: Bankruptcies; Dish bought DBSD and TerreStar for ~$2.86B combined in 2012
lesson: The upgrade from satellite to terrestrial use came after the original holders failed; the distressed buyer captured it.

name: Metricom (Ricochet)
outcome_value: Chapter 11 in July 2001; assets sold for ~$8M (prior knowledge)
lesson: A failed business model and technology overwhelm whatever the spectrum is worth.

name: India 2024 spectrum auction
outcome_value: ~INR 11,341 crore sold (prior knowledge)
lesson: With three operators that had bought heavily in 2022, oversupply and high reserve prices left most spectrum unsold.

name: Canada 3500 vs 3800 MHz auctions
holder: ISED (seller); Rogers, Bell, Telus and others
outcome_value: 3800 MHz auction C$2.16B (2023, prior knowledge)
lesson: More supply of a similar band sells far cheaper; the early buyers paid the scarcity premium.

name: Grain Management 800 MHz resale to SpaceX
spectrum: 800 MHz, up to 14 MHz paired nationwide
cost_basis: Acquired from T-Mobile in Aug 2026 for cash plus Grain's 600 MHz (thinly sourced)
outcome_value: Sale to SpaceX agreed 2026-10-08; terms undisclosed; FCC approval pending
lesson: A specialist intermediary with carrier relationships can capture the spread by moving low-band from a carrier to a satellite buyer.

name: Broadcasters in the 600 MHz incentive auction
holder: TV station owners, including speculators who bought stations before the auction
cost_basis: Existing broadcast licences (station purchase prices vary)
outcome_value: ~$10B paid to relinquishing stations; auction ~$19.8B gross (prior knowledge)
lesson: A regulator-run repurposing paid incumbents directly; the gains were set by auction design, not market scarcity alone.
